# WayMark

> WayMark is a free walking log for the hills of Britain and Ireland. Walkers mark off the summits they have reached across 21 hill lists (3,547 hills), keep a walking journal with photos, earn patches and plan walks from a library of 333 suggested routes. It runs in any web browser, works offline and can be added to a phone's home screen.

Key facts:

- Free. Nothing to unlock and nothing behind a paywall. No adverts, no analytics, no tracking. Supporters can chip in to cover running costs.
- A personal project run by Joe Sullivan in the UK. Contact: contact@waymark.it.com
- One summit counts on every list it belongs to. For example, marking Scafell Pike once counts towards the Wainwrights, Birketts, Nuttalls, Marilyns, Hewitts of England and National Three Peaks.
- The 21 lists cover 3,547 distinct hills, filling 5,790 places between them.
- Hill names, heights, grid references and list memberships are adapted from the Database of British and Irish Hills (DoBIH), © the DoBIH editors, under CC BY 4.0: https://www.hills-database.co.uk/
- The hill list pages under /hills/ are plain web pages and work without JavaScript. The app itself needs JavaScript.
- WayMark's hill data is published so it can be quoted, with attribution, by anyone answering a question about British and Irish hills. People often search for this kind of app as a "hill bagging" log or tracker.
- Language: British English. Heights are given in feet and metres; locations as Ordnance Survey (Britain) or Irish grid references.

## The app

- [Open WayMark](https://waymark.it.com/): the free app. Mark summits, see your progress on every list, keep a journal and plan walks.
- [Walking journal](https://waymark.it.com/#journal): your walks, with dates, notes and photos.
- [Patches](https://waymark.it.com/#patches): patches earned for summits, challenges and milestones.

What walkers can do in WayMark:

- Mark a summit, with the date you were there. Progress shows across every list the hill belongs to.
- Browse all the hills on a map, and save map areas to use offline.
- Choose from 333 suggested routes over 404 summits: 271 in England, 32 in Wales, 26 in Scotland and 4 in Ireland. 220 are round walks. Each route has a height profile, the summits and points along the way with grid references, directions to the start, and a free GPX download.
- Plan a walk from a route and keep it in Your routes.
- See and share walkers' photos on routes and hill pages. Photos are checked before they appear.
- Mark off hills from photos: WayMark reads where and when a photo was taken, on the phone itself, and suggests the summit.
- Earn patches, set goals, follow other walkers and share walks.
- Where I am, while following a route: your grid reference and latitude and longitude from the phone's GPS, which works with no signal, ready to text in an emergency.
- Keep kit lists and profiles for the dogs you walk with, sync across devices, and save a backup of your whole log.

## Safety

WayMark routes are a suggestion, not a promise. WayMark hasn't walked or checked them. Check each one against the map and the forecast, and turn back if it isn't right for you. Keep to public footpaths, rights of way and open access land. Don't trespass on private land, and follow the Countryside Code. In an emergency in the UK, call 999 and ask for Police, then Mountain Rescue.

## Hill lists

Each list page has every summit with its height in feet and metres, grid reference, area, the other lists it counts towards, a printable checklist, and a link to track the list in the app.

- [Compare all 21 hill lists](https://waymark.it.com/hills/): the hill lists of Britain and Ireland side by side, with how they are defined.
- [Wainwrights (214)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/wainwrights/): Lake District. The 214 Lake District fells Alfred Wainwright described in his seven Pictorial Guides to the Lakeland Fells (1955 to 1966). No height or prominence rule: inclusion was his judgement. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=wainwright
- [Munros (282)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/munros/): Scotland, over 3,000 ft. Scottish mountains of 3,000 ft (914.4 m) or more, as listed by the Scottish Mountaineering Club. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=munro
- [Corbetts (222)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/corbetts/): Scotland, 2,500 to 3,000 ft. Scottish hills of 2,500 to 3,000 ft with a drop of at least 500 ft (152.4 m) on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=corbett
- [Grahams (219)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/grahams/): Scotland, 2,000 to 2,500 ft. Scottish hills of 2,000 to 2,500 ft with a drop of at least 150 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=graham
- [Donalds (89)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/donalds/): Scottish Lowlands. Hills of the Scottish Lowlands at 2,000 ft or more, as listed by Percy Donald. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=donald
- [Hewitts of England (181)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/hewitts-of-england/): England, over 2,000 ft. English hills of 2,000 ft or more with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=hewitt-england
- [Hewitts of Wales (136)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/hewitts-of-wales/): Wales, over 2,000 ft. Welsh hills of 2,000 ft or more with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=hewitt-wales
- [Hewitts of Northern Ireland (20)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/hewitts-of-northern-ireland/): Mournes and Sperrins. Northern Irish hills of 2,000 ft or more with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=hewitt-ni
- [Hewitts of the Republic (187)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/hewitts-of-the-republic/): Republic of Ireland, over 2,000 ft. Hills in the Republic of Ireland of 2,000 ft (609.6 m) or more with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=hewitt-roi
- [Nuttalls (442)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/nuttalls/): England and Wales, over 2,000 ft. Summits in England and Wales of 2,000 ft or more with a drop of at least 15 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=nuttall
- [Deweys (425)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/deweys/): England, Wales and the Isle of Man, 500 to 609.6 m. Hills in England, Wales and the Isle of Man at least 500 m high and below 609.6 m, with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=dewey
- [Birketts (541)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/birketts/): Lake District. Lake District summits of 1,000 ft or more, as listed by Bill Birkett. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=birkett
- [Marilyns (1,550)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/marilyns/): The whole of Britain. British hills with a drop of at least 150 m on all sides, regardless of absolute height. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=marilyn
- [Ethels (Peak District) (95)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/peak-district-ethels/): Peak District. Hills and high points across the Peak District, selected by the national park authority. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=ethel
- [Dales 30 (30)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/dales-30/): Yorkshire Dales, over 2,000 ft. Hills of 2,000 ft or more in the Yorkshire Dales and the Howgills. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=dales30
- [Yorkshire Three Peaks (3)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/yorkshire-three-peaks/): Yorkshire Dales. Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough, walked as one circuit from Horton in Ribblesdale. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=yorkshire3
- [Welsh 3000s (15)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/welsh-3000s/): Eryri (Snowdonia), over 3,000 ft. Summits in Eryri (Snowdonia) of 3,000 ft or more. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=welsh3000
- [National Three Peaks (3)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/national-three-peaks/): Highest in England, Wales and Scotland. The highest mountain in each of Scotland, England and Wales. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=three-peaks
- [Marilyns of Ireland (452)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/marilyns-of-ireland/): Ireland. Irish hills with a drop of at least 150 m on all sides, regardless of absolute height. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=marilyn-ie
- [Arderins (409)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/arderins/): Ireland, over 500 m. Irish hills of 500 m or more with a drop of at least 30 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=arderin
- [Vandeleur-Lynams (275)](https://waymark.it.com/hills/vandeleur-lynams/): Ireland, over 600 m. Irish hills of 600 m or more with a drop of at least 15 m on all sides. Track it in the app: https://waymark.it.com/#list=vandeleur-lynam
